mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A's shots FOR (RECENT_5) is materially below its ALL_PRIOR mean AND Team A's shots AGAINST (RECENT_5) is materially above its ALL_PRIOR mean simultaneously. Measure whether the joint regime predicts a different total-shots and shots-on-target distribution than either single-observable drift alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both Team A's attacking shot output falls and its defensive shot allowance rises jointly, the combined shots-on-target total for the match is suppressed relative to what either single-observable trend would imply independently.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume collapse in recent matches (RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR) co-occurs with a simultaneous surge in shots conceded, suggesting a joint deterioration in both attacking and defensive shot-generation balance. The joint direction of these two observables — shots FOR falling while shots AGAINST rises — may predict a compressed total-shots environment differently than either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots FOR and shots AGAINST) both shifting in the same adverse direction simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable with one conditioning band; it requires measuring the intersection of two observable drift signals.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the possession-holding team (Team A, historically ~52%) faces an opponent (Team B) whose shots-FOR rate is well below competition average but whose shots-AGAINST rate is well above it. Measure whether corner-kick volume for the possession-dominant side rises with this asymmetric shot-generation imbalance across the two teams.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Corner kicks for the possession-dominant team rise when the opponent's defensive shot-allowance rate is high relative to its own attacking shot rate — i.e., the asymmetry between Team B's shots FOR and shots AGAINST amplifies corner generation for Team A beyond what possession alone predicts.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession share is structurally higher than Team B's (both all-prior and venue-split), yet Team A's shots FOR are only marginally above competition average while Team B allows far more shots than it generates. The asymmetric relationship between possession dominance (Team A) and shot-generation efficiency (Team B's low shots FOR vs high shots AGAINST) may jointly determine corner-kick volume differently than possession or shots alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a cross-team asymmetric relationship between two distinct observables (possession for one team, shots-FOR vs shots-AGAINST imbalance for the other). It cannot be reduced to a single observable mirror or a single conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) Team A's corner-kicks FOR RECENT_5 being materially below its ALL_PRIOR mean, AND (b) Team B's corner-kicks AGAINST ALL_PRIOR being above competition average. Measure whether the combination of attacker drought plus permissive-opponent context predicts a reversion in corner volume or sustained suppression, compared to either condition alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's recent corner output is suppressed but the opponent historically concedes above-average corners, the joint regime tests whether corner volume reverts toward the opponent's concession baseline or remains anchored to the attacker's recent form — i.e., which dimension dominates in the joint conditioning.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner-kick production has collapsed in RECENT_5 (2.6) relative to its ALL_PRIOR mean (5.57), while Team B concedes corners at a rate (5.64 ALL_PRIOR, 4.4 RECENT_5) that is above competition average. The joint condition of Team A's corner-generation drought AND Team B's corner-concession profile creates a two-dimensional regime that may predict whether corner totals revert or remain suppressed, beyond what either team's single-observable trend implies.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct temporal windows (RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR) for the same observable across two different teams, testing which regime dominates. It is not a single observable with one band; it is a two-team, two-window joint conditioning.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where a team's fouls FOR (RECENT_5) is materially below its ALL_PRIOR mean while its cards_2h FOR (ALL_PRIOR) remains above competition average. Measure whether second-half card volume is better predicted by the joint relationship between foul rate and card rate than by either observable alone — specifically testing whether a low-foul, high-card regime exists as a distinct pattern.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half cards remain elevated even as foul volume declines, suggesting a non-linear (threshold) relationship where card issuance per foul rises when foul volume falls — i.e., cards_2h does not scale linearly with fouls in this regime.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's second-half cards rate (cards_2h FOR: 1.663) is the highest among both teams and above competition average (1.403), while Team B's fouls FOR have dropped sharply in RECENT_5 (9.6) versus ALL_PRIOR (12.337). This divergence between a structurally elevated second-half card rate and a recent foul-rate decline creates a joint observable pattern: whether second-half cards are driven by foul volume or by a threshold effect where fewer but more dangerous fouls yield disproportionate cards.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This tests a non-linear / threshold relationship between two distinct observables (fouls and cards_2h) rather than treating either in isolation. It also involves a cross-window divergence (RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR) on one observable while the other remains structurally elevated — a joint two-observable, two-window conditioning not covered by any single-observable baseline.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) Team A's goals FOR being back-loaded (second-half mean exceeds first-half mean), AND (b) Team B's goals AGAINST being back-loaded (second-half concession mean exceeds first-half concession mean). Measure whether the alignment of both teams' second-half goal tendencies predicts elevated second-half goal volume beyond what either team's half-split alone would imply.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the attacking team's scoring is back-loaded AND the defending team's concession is also back-loaded, second-half goal volume rises above what either team's individual half-split would predict independently — the two asymmetries reinforce each other.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goals FOR split between first half (0.688) and second half (0.806) shows a back-loaded scoring pattern, while Team B's goals AGAINST split shows the opposite asymmetry — conceding more in the second half (0.910) than the first (0.629). The joint within-match half-level asymmetry across both teams' goal profiles (Team A scores more in H2; Team B concedes more in H2) may predict second-half goal volume differently than full-match averages or either team's half-split in isolation.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint conditioning on two distinct teams' within-match half-level splits for the same observable, testing whether the alignment of both asymmetries produces a compounding effect. It is not a single observable with one band, nor a simple home/away or recent/prior split — it is a two-team, within-match period interaction.
